pool_config.pool_brief: Build a loop-driven data processor for a Nigerian business context. Your solution must use: a for loop with an index, a for...of loop, a for...in loop, at least one break or continue, and a while loop with a safety-net counter. All variables must use const or let (no var).

projects.title: Jumia Order Dashboard
projects.scenario: Build a loop-based order analytics tool for a Jumia seller. Process an array of 6 orders with id, customer, amount, and status fields.
requirements: Use a for loop with index to print a numbered order list: 'Order 1 of 6: Amara Obi — ₦4500'
Use a for...of loop with continue to skip cancelled orders and sum the revenue from delivered and pending orders
Use a for...of loop with break to find and print the first pending order
Use a for...in loop to print all keys and values of the first order object
Use a while loop with a max-iteration counter to simulate processing orders until a ₦20,000 shipping budget runs out (₦500 per order)

Open the browser console to see your output.

projects.title: Publica Academy Grade Processor
projects.scenario: Build a grade processing system for a Publica Academy cohort. Process an array of 6 student records with name, score, and module fields.
requirements: Use a for loop with index to print each student as: 'Student 1: Amara Obi — Module: JavaScript — Score: 88'
Use a for...of loop with continue to skip students who scored below 50, and accumulate total marks for passing students
Use a for...of loop with break to find the first student who scored above 90
Use a for...in loop to print every field of the highest-scoring student object
Use a while loop with a max counter to simulate awarding certificates one by one until a ₦5,000 printing budget runs out (₦800 per certificate)

projects.title: PiggyVest Transaction Analyser
projects.scenario: Build a transaction analysis tool for a PiggyVest savings account. Process an array of 6 transactions with id, type, amount, and category fields.
requirements: Use a for loop with index to print each transaction as: 'Txn 1: deposit — ₦5000 (savings)'
Use a for...of loop with continue to skip withdrawals and accumulate total deposits
Use a for...of loop with break to find the first transaction with amount greater than ₦10,000
Use a for...in loop to print every field of the largest transaction object
Use a while loop with a safety counter to simulate draining the account balance (starting at ₦25,000, withdrawing ₦4,000 each iteration, maximum 10 iterations)

projects.title: Paystack Payment Batch Processor
projects.scenario: Build a payment batch processor for a Paystack merchant. Process an array of 6 payments with id, merchant, amount, and status fields.
requirements: Use a for loop with index to print each payment as: 'Payment 1 of 6: Shoprite — ₦15000 (success)'
Use a for...of loop with continue to skip failed payments and accumulate total successful revenue
Use a for...of loop with break to stop processing at the first failed payment and log which payment caused the halt
Use a for...in loop to print every field of the first failed payment object
Use a while loop with a safety counter to simulate verifying payments one by one until all are confirmed or a 5-attempt limit is reached

projects.title: Bolt Driver Trip Report
projects.scenario: Build a trip report generator for a Bolt driver. Process an array of 6 trips with id, driver, fare, distance, and rating fields.
requirements: Use a for loop with index to print each trip as: 'Trip 1 of 6: Gbenga Musa — ₦1800 — 4.8★'
Use a for...of loop with continue to skip trips with rating below 4.0, and accumulate total fare from high-rated trips
Use a for...of loop with break to find the highest-fare trip (stop when a trip with fare > ₦3000 is found)
Use a for...in loop to print every field of the highest-fare trip object
Use a while loop with a safety counter to simulate a driver completing trips until a 12-hour daily limit (each trip takes 1.5 hours, maximum 10 iterations)

descriptors.full: Classic for loop correctly uses index, for...of cleanly iterates values, both produce correct output
descriptors.partial: One loop type works correctly but the other has errors or is missing
descriptors.none: Both for loop types are missing or produce incorrect output

descriptors.full: continue correctly skips items and the loop processes remaining items, break correctly exits after finding the first match
descriptors.partial: One keyword used correctly, the other missing or incorrectly applied
descriptors.none: Neither break nor continue used, or both produce incorrect behavior

descriptors.full: for...in correctly iterates object keys using bracket notation, while loop includes a max-iteration counter and handles both exit conditions
descriptors.partial: One of the two works correctly, the other has errors or is missing the safety counter
descriptors.none: Both are missing or produce incorrect output

descriptors.full: const/let used correctly throughout, loop variable names are clear (order, student, tx etc.), output format matches requirements exactly
descriptors.partial: Minor naming issues or small format discrepancies
descriptors.none: var used, unclear variable names, or output is significantly malformed
